channel.title: For All Beings
channel.description: Source-verified Buddhist teaching excerpts with full attribution.

item.title: Yeshe Tsogyal (traditional attribution; Pema Lingpa terma) — Yeshe Tsogyal’s Prayer
item.description:
May any connection we have be of deepest benefit and meaning.
Yeshe Tsogyal (traditional attribution; Pema Lingpa terma) Translation: Rigpa Translations, 2014; version 1.2-20210916 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/pema-lingpa/yeshe-tsogyals-prayer Aspiration to benefit beings through every connection; attributed speech preserved in a later treasure revelation.

item.title: Seung Sahn — True God, True Buddha
item.description:
Open your mouth and it's already a mistake. But our job is to help all beings.
Seung Sahn Translation: English teaching as published by Kwan Um School; no translator credited https://kwanumzen.org/teaching-library/1990/12/01/true-god-true-buddha Paradox about speech and transmission immediately resolved through teaching for others' benefit.

item.title: Ajahn Chah — In Simple Terms
item.description:
Practice by letting go. Don’t hold on. Or if you hold on, don’t hold on tight.
Ajahn Chah Translation: Thanissaro Bhikkhu, revised edition, introduction May 2013 https://www.dhammatalks.org/books/InSimpleTerms/Section0006.html Holding provisionally to investigate then setting down; not indifference.

item.title: Somā — Soma Sutta (SN 5.2)
item.description:
What difference does being a woman make when the mind's well-centered, when knowledge is progressing, seeing clearly, rightly, into the Dhamma.
Somā Translation: Thanissaro Bhikkhu, 1998; ATI 2013 https://accesstoinsight.org/tipitaka/sn/sn05/sn05.002.than.html The nun refutes Māra’s claim that women cannot attain.

item.title: Attributed to Padmasambhava — My view is higher than the sky…
item.description:
My view is higher than the sky, My attention to the karmic process finer than grains of flour.
Attributed to Padmasambhava Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2004, revised 2025 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/indian-masters/padmasambhava/view-is-higher Source explicitly labels attribution; ultimate view coupled with karmic care.

item.title: Mipham — Mental Purification in Practice
item.description:
Teaching is not paramount, meditation is. When meditating don’t teach but learn deeply. To teach without meditating is to be like a parrot.
Mipham Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2021; v1.2–20250115 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/mipham/putting-analytical-meditation-into-practice Emphasizes analytical practice, not anti-intellectualism.

item.title: Shikai Zuiko — Wherever You Stand 9: Who: Dajian Huineng Part 2
item.description:
When you notice anything whatsoever, notice everything else that’s going on without naming it.
Shikai Zuiko Translation: English teaching, February 2, 2013; no translation https://wwzc.org/wherever-you-stand-9-who-dajian-huineng-part-2/ Actual speaker is modern teacher Shikai Zuiko, not Huineng whom talk discusses.

item.title: Patrul Rinpoche — Self-Liberating Meditation
item.description:
Mind has always been empty. There is no need to search. It is the very one who searches.
Patrul Rinpoche Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2018; version 1.5–20250414 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/patrul-rinpoche/self-liberating-meditation Opening instructions identify the searcher itself as mind; surrounding passage instructs settling without distraction.

item.title: Tilopa — The Ganges Mahāmudrā Instructions
item.description:
When you attain non-attainment, you attain Mahāmudrā.
Tilopa Translation: Ina Bieler; edited by Kay Candler; revised 2023 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/indian-masters/tilopa/ganges-mahamudra-instruction Final line of verse 19, following retreat and non-meditation instructions; Tilopa addresses Naropa.

item.title: Avalokiteśvara in the Heart Sūtra — Heart Sūtra
item.description:
Form is empty; emptiness is form. Emptiness is not other than form; form is not other than emptiness.
Avalokiteśvara in the Heart Sūtra Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2019; v1.3–20220729 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/words-of-the-buddha/heart-sutra Actual speaker Avalokiteśvara, teaching through Buddha’s power.

item.title: Longchen Rabjam — Immaculate Radiance: A Testament
item.description:
Phenomena in their variety are like reflections in a mirror: Appearing yet empty—and there’s no emptiness but this.
Longchen Rabjam Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2024; version 1.1–20240503 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/longchen-rabjam/immaculate-radiance-testament Appearance and emptiness presented inseparably; subsequent lines advise certainty rather than naive reification.

item.title: Sera Khandro — I Don’t Believe in Samsara… Spiritual Advice
item.description:
Nothing truly exists. Everything is empty. Nothing is non-existent. Everything is very clear.
Sera Khandro Translation: Christina Monson, 2022 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/sera-khandro/spiritual-advice-dont-believe-in-samsara-etc Emptiness paired with clarity, avoiding nihilistic truncation.

item.title: Dōgen — Actualizing the Fundamental Point (Genjo-koan)
item.description:
No trace of realization remains, and this no-trace continues endlessly.
Dōgen Translation: Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi; revised at San Francisco Zen Center https://media.berkeleyzencenter.org/GenjoKoan-Kaz.pdf Forgetting self and actualization by myriad things; continuing practice.

item.title: Śāntideva — Bodhicaryāvatāra 9.34, quoted in Khenpo Petsé’s Meditation on the Great Middle Way
item.description:
When neither entity nor non-entity Remain before the mind, There is no position left to take, And it rests in non-conceptual peace.
Śāntideva Translation: Cortland Dahl under Khenpo Sherab Sangpo, 2007; Lotsawa House 2022 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/khenpo-petse/meditation-on-great-middle-way After analysis of dependent arising; contextual sequel connects insight to compassion.

item.title: Mipham Rinpoche — The Essence of Mind
item.description:
The actual nature of things is inconceivable and inexpressible.
Mipham Rinpoche Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2016; version 1.2–20220421 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/mipham/essence-of-mind Opening statement followed by illustrative instructions; not a rejection of teaching or practice.

item.title: Rongzom Chökyi Zangpo — The Black Snake Discourse
item.description:
We only repudiate your inferior metaphysical views without establishing any superior point of our own.
Rongzom Chökyi Zangpo Translation: David Higgins, 2023 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/rongzom-chokyi-zangpo/black-snake-discourse Polemical response within vehicle classification, rejecting a metaphysical thesis of one’s own.

item.title: The Buddha — Bāhiya Sutta (Udāna 1.10)
item.description:
When there is no you there, you are neither here nor yonder nor between the two.
The Buddha Translation: Thanissaro Bhikkhu, 1994; Access to Insight edition 2012 https://accesstoinsight.org/tipitaka/kn/ud/ud.1.10.than.html Excerpt from the Buddha’s instruction to Bāhiya concerning seeing, hearing, sensing and cognizing without identification.

item.title: The Buddha — Nibbāna Sutta (Ud 8.3)
item.description:
There is, monks, an unborn — unbecome — unmade — unfabricated.
The Buddha Translation: Thanissaro Bhikkhu, 2012 https://accesstoinsight.org/tipitaka/kn/ud/ud.8.03.than.html Unconditioned as escape from the conditioned.

item.title: The Buddha — Nibbāna Sutta: Unbinding (Ud 8.1)
item.description:
And there, I say, there is neither coming, nor going, nor staying; neither passing away nor arising: unestablished, unevolving, without support [mental object].
The Buddha Translation: Thanissaro Bhikkhu, 2012 https://accesstoinsight.org/tipitaka/kn/ud/ud.8.01.than.html Description of unbinding; bracketed phrase is translator’s wording; footnote markers omitted.

item.title: Padmasambhava (attributed) — Unstained by objects of perception…
item.description:
Unstained by objects of perception, Unspoilt by apprehending thought, Sustaining naked, empty awareness— This is the wisdom of all the buddhas!
Padmasambhava (attributed) Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2004; revised 2025 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/indian-masters/padmasambhava/unstained-by-objects Source attributes these words to Padmasambhava in a pure vision of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo; not represented as a historical transcript.

item.title: Dudjom Lingpa — Meditation Advice to the Nun Chötso
item.description:
Settle without holding to a technique. Be done with that. Just relax—at ease—letting go of distraction and meditation.
Dudjom Lingpa Translation: Ringu Tulku and Holly Gayley, 2018; revised 2022 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/dudjom-lingpa/advice-to-nun-chotso Advice for an experienced meditator; the conclusion explicitly preserves ethical discernment.

item.title: Sera Khandro — Alpha Purity
item.description:
Alpha-pure, inexpressible awareness, Beyond colour and characteristics— Carefully analyze with intelligence. Demolish the “I” or self at its source.
Sera Khandro Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2022 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/sera-khandro/alpha-purity-advice The 'I' means self-grasping; Tibetan alphabet acrostic rendered in English abecedarian form.

item.title: Third Karmapa, Rangjung Dorje — Aspiration of the Mahāmudrā of Definitive Meaning
item.description:
Mind itself is without mind, empty of mind’s essence— Empty yet unrestricted, appearing in any way at all.
Third Karmapa, Rangjung Dorje Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2020, revised 2024 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/third-karmapa-rangjung-dorje/mahamudra-aspiration Emptiness and unobstructed appearance together, not a claim of nonexistence.

item.title: Longchen Rabjam — The Ultimate Wish-Fulfilling Essence
item.description:
In naturally arisen awareness, boundless and unconfined, Undo the knot that retains the aspects of ordinary mind.
Longchen Rabjam Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2024 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/longchen-rabjam/ultimate-wish-fulfilling-essence Concluding verse of Dzogchen instructions; text marked for transmission holders, excerpt is a general concluding aspiration.

item.title: Padampa Sangye, quoted by Dodrupchen — Transforming Suffering and Happiness into Enlightenment
item.description:
We human beings can cope with a lot of suffering, But very little happiness.
Padampa Sangye, quoted by Dodrupchen Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2006, based on Rigpa Translations https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/dodrupchen-III/transforming-suffering-and-happiness Warns about complacency when happy; text teaches use of both happiness and suffering.

item.title: Rongzom Chökyi Zangpo — Establishing Appearances as Divine
item.description:
Distinction between continuums of self and other, moreover, are divided in and by persons; they are not qualitatively different phenomena.
Rongzom Chökyi Zangpo Translation: Dominic Sur, 2024; revised 2026 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/rongzom-chokyi-zangpo/establishing-appearances-as-divine Argument concerning consciousness and the divinity of appearances; source grammar preserved.

item.title: Marpa Lotsāwa — Song quoted in Mahāmudrā Way of Resting by Fifth Shamarpa
item.description:
This mental consciousness, reifying what is internal, Is realized to be unborn dharmakāya.
Marpa Lotsāwa Translation: Joseph McClellan, 2026 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/fifth-shamarpa/mahamudra-way-of-resting Marpa summarizes Maitripa's instructions; quoted by Fifth Shamarpa, not misattributed to him.

item.title: Nāropa — A Spiritual Song on the Eight Supreme Difficulties
item.description:
When you discover the taste of co-emergence, Saṃsāra is overwhelmed, transformed into great bliss.
Nāropa Translation: Sean Ross, 2024 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/indian-masters/naropa/eight-difficulties-song A song attributed to Nāropa preserved in Marpa’s collected works vol1 p76.

item.title: Padmasambhava in Pema Ledrel Tsal’s terma — The Golden Garland of Nectar: Questions and Answers
item.description:
Tsogyal, there are many who claim to have realized emptiness, but few who have realized the ultimate nature.
Padmasambhava in Pema Ledrel Tsal’s terma Translation: Adam Pearcey, 2026; provisional translation https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/pema-ledrel-tsal/golden-garland-questions-answers Dialogue warns against sterile emptiness and abandoning compassion; treasure attribution, not historical transcript.

item.title: Attributed to Milarepa — In horror of death…
item.description:
Capturing the fortress of the deathless unending nature of mind. Now all fear of death is over and done.
Attributed to Milarepa Translation: Rigpa Translations; version on Lotsawa House verified 2026-09-28 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/milarepa/in-horror-of-death Preceding lines describe retreat and repeated contemplation of uncertain death; not a claim of bodily immortality.

item.title: Man Gong — Prajna Ship, quoted in Pilgrimage to India, 2011
item.description:
You and I are not two, not one. Only your stupid thinking is nonstop.
Man Gong Translation: Kwan Um School English version; translator uncredited https://kwanumzen.org/teaching-library/2012/10/10/pilgrimage-to-india-2011 Article explains not attaching to thinking, rather than eliminating the thinking mind.

item.title: Nāgārjuna (traditional attribution) — In Praise of the Stūpas at the Eight Great Sacred Places
item.description:
I bow to all dharmakāyas abiding At the eight stūpas of Śākyamuni, In the ten directions, and elsewhere— I humbly pay homage, always, to peace!
Nāgārjuna (traditional attribution) Translation: Monica Thunder and Peter Woods, Samye Translations; v1.0–20230907 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/indian-masters/nagarjuna/praise-stupas-eight-places-01 Traditional Tengyur attribution, Toh 1133, Derge vol1 fol81b3–82a3. Homage to peace.

item.title: Padmasambhava (Dorje Lingpa treasure attribution) — The Final Words of Padmasambhava / Sacred Refined Essence Instruction; included in Dakini Teachings
item.description:
The most vital point is therefore to sustain your practice undistractedly from this very moment.
Padmasambhava (Dorje Lingpa treasure attribution) Translation: Erik Pema Kunsang https://levekunst.com/the-final-words-of-padmasambhava/ Instruction to Yeshe Tsogyal on practice, death and the bardo; traditional treasure attribution to Padmasambhava, revealed by Dorje Lingpa. Article credited to the translator; colophon explicitly credits his translation. No independent historical-transcript claim.

item.title: The Buddha (canonical attribution) — Dhammapada
item.description:
For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.
The Buddha (canonical attribution) Translation: F. Max Müller https://www.gutenberg.org/files/2017/2017-h/2017-h.htm Complete numbered verse checked with neighboring verses in the source. Historical translation; retain its wording without modernization. Mix sparingly with the prioritized Tibetan translations rather than publish as a continuous book sequence.

item.title: The Buddha (canonical attribution) — Dhammapada
item.description:
As the bee collects nectar and departs without injuring the flower, or its colour or scent, so let a sage dwell in his village.
The Buddha (canonical attribution) Translation: F. Max Müller https://www.gutenberg.org/files/2017/2017-h/2017-h.htm Complete numbered verse checked with neighboring verses in the source. Historical translation; retain its wording without modernization. Mix sparingly with the prioritized Tibetan translations rather than publish as a continuous book sequence.

item.title: The Buddha (canonical attribution) — Dhammapada
item.description:
As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
The Buddha (canonical attribution) Translation: F. Max Müller https://www.gutenberg.org/files/2017/2017-h/2017-h.htm Complete numbered verse checked with neighboring verses in the source. Historical translation; retain its wording without modernization. Mix sparingly with the prioritized Tibetan translations rather than publish as a continuous book sequence.

item.title: The Buddha (canonical attribution) — Dhammapada
item.description:
Wise people, after they have listened to the laws, become serene, like a deep, smooth, and still lake.
The Buddha (canonical attribution) Translation: F. Max Müller https://www.gutenberg.org/files/2017/2017-h/2017-h.htm Complete numbered verse checked with neighboring verses in the source. Historical translation; retain its wording without modernization. Mix sparingly with the prioritized Tibetan translations rather than publish as a continuous book sequence.

item.title: Gampopa (as presented by Erik Pema Kunsang) — The Eleven Instructions of Gampopa
item.description:
Don’t reject compassion, since it is the basis for helping others.
Gampopa (as presented by Erik Pema Kunsang) Translation: Erik Pema Kunsang (English presentation; no separate translation credit on page) https://levekunst.com/the-eleven-instructions-of-gampopa/ Article explicitly attributes the list to Gampopa. This compassion instruction is self-contained. Article author is Erik Pema Kunsang; credit the presentation rather than invent a separate edition or translation colophon.

item.title: Tsoknyi Rinpoche — Carefree Dignity
item.description:
Someone who has realized emptiness is naturally compassionate, and doesn’t close off and become concerned with only him or herself.
Tsoknyi Rinpoche Translation: Erik Pema Kunsang and Marcia Binder Schmidt; edited by Kerry Moran https://levekunst.com/carefree-dignity/ Tsoknyi Rinpoche speaking about the example of his father Tulku Urgyen. Actual speaker is Tsoknyi, not Tulku Urgyen or the article byline. Colophon credits translators, editor, and 1998 copyright.

item.title: Nyoshul Khen Rinpoche — The Perfect Mirror (poem in Erik Pema Kunsang’s article)
item.description:
Let unmoved mind look into itself.
Nyoshul Khen Rinpoche Translation: Erik Pema Kunsang https://levekunst.com/the-perfect-mirror/ Kunsang explicitly introduces this as his new translation of Nyoshul Khenpo’s poem. This line is from the poem, not the translator’s surrounding commentary; nondual presence is the stated context.

item.title: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche — The True View
item.description:
Emptiness without compassion is never taught to be the true path of enlightenment.
Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche Translation: Erik Pema Kunsang (editor credited; separate translator not specified on page) https://levekunst.com/the-true-view/ Oral teaching excerpt introduced as Tulku Urgyen; compassion and emptiness as inseparable. Article notes partial extraction from Treasures from Juniper Ridge; track that work cumulatively. Not a recording.

item.title: Sera Khandro — Concise Spiritual Advice
item.description:
In your behavior, love beings from all six realms as your own children.
Sera Khandro Translation: Christina Monson, 2020 https://www.lotsawahouse.org/tibetan-masters/sera-khandro/concise-spiritual-advice Advice joins conduct, bodhicitta, meditation and action/results; direct authorial advice.

item.title: Muttā (canonical attribution) — Therīgāthā 1.11
item.description:
Having uprooted the craving that leads to becoming, I'm set free from aging & death.
Muttā (canonical attribution) Translation: Thanissaro Bhikkhu https://accesstoinsight.org/tipitaka/kn/thig/thig.01.00x.than.html The nun celebrates freedom after describing release from domestic drudgery. This is her own first-person verse, not advice addressed to her.

item.title: Avalokiteśvara (speaker in the sūtra) — The Heart of the Perfection of Wisdom, the Blessed Mother (Toh 21)
item.description:
Form is empty. Emptiness is form. Emptiness is not other than form, and form is also not other than emptiness.
Avalokiteśvara (speaker in the sūtra) Translation: Dharmachakra Translation Committee; translation produced by Catherine Dalton and Andreas Doctor https://84000.co/translation/toh21 Avalokiteśvara explains the five aggregates’ lack of intrinsic nature in answer to Śāriputra’s question about practicing the perfection of wisdom. Actual speaker is Avalokiteśvara, not the Buddha.

item.title: Sela (canonical attribution) — Sela Sutta (SN 5.9)
item.description:
This doll isn't self-made, nor is this misery made by another. In dependence on a cause it comes into play. With the dissolution of the cause it ceases.
Sela (canonical attribution) Translation: Thanissaro Bhikkhu https://www.accesstoinsight.org/tipitaka/sn/sn05/sn05.009.than.html After recognizing Māra’s challenge about who made the “doll,” the nun Sela answers that the aggregates arise dependent on causes and cease when those causes dissolve. These are Sela’s words, not Māra’s.

item.title: Ārya Nāgārjuna — The Heart of Dependent Origination, verse 7
item.description:
In this, there is not a thing to be removed, Nor the slightest thing to be added. It is looking perfectly into reality itself, And when reality is seen, complete liberation.
Ārya Nāgārjuna Translation: Adam Pearcey https://www.lotsawahouse.org/indian-masters/nagarjuna/heart-dependent-origination The verse describes seeing reality itself, not a thing to add or remove; retained as a single verse.

item.title: Zen Master Dae Kwang — Why does the Buddha have big ears?
item.description:
It was not to solve some intellectual puzzle, or even to take away his own suffering. Rather, it was for all beings.
Zen Master Dae Kwang Translation: No translator credited; original English teaching https://kwanumzen.org/teaching-library/1992/02/01/why-does-the-buddha-have-big-ears Dae Kwang explains the Buddha’s search as directed toward the welfare of all beings rather than solving an intellectual puzzle or ending only his own suffering.

item.title: James Low — Staying open in a shut down world
item.description:
The direct one is to start from where we actually are. And the indirect paths start from where we think we are.
Spoken in English. Transcript credited to Lea Pabst. A teaching contrasting direct and indirect approaches to practice. The official page includes the recording and transcript. Transcript: https://simplybeing.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/538-2020-May-Zoom-Staying-open-in-a-shut-down-world-LPabst-Webready.pdf

item.title: Lama Lena — Working with Thoughts — Part 1
item.description:
It is extremely important that you not take my word for this. Go look.
Spoken in English. Official archive transcript; transcriber uncredited. An invitation to examine thoughts directly. The linked section begins at 18:56; the quoted words occur within it. Transcript: https://lamalenateachings.com/working-with-thoughts/
